title: FinFETs and the MOS Capacitor
intro: Two topics that round off the device chapter: the three-dimensional FinFET used below about 20 nm, and how a MOS structure behaves as a capacitor (Razavi, Appendices 2.5 and 2.6).

blocks.text: As planar channel lengths fell below roughly 20 nm the gate lost control of the channel: leakage and channel-length modulation grew. Recent nodes therefore stand the channel up as a thin vertical fin of silicon, cover it with a gate dielectric and wrap the gate over its top and both sides. With the gate holding the channel from three sides, the FinFET has less channel-length modulation and less subthreshold leakage, and its I/V curves come closer to the square law again, which makes the simple model more useful.

blocks.alt: Perspective drawing of a FinFET on a flat blue substrate. A thin, tall green silicon fin runs from the source block at the front left to the drain block at the back right. A red gate crosses over the middle of the fin, covering both of its side walls, and a pointer labels the fin.
blocks.caption: A FinFET. The channel is the fin's surface under the gate, so the gate controls it from more than one side. Image: Irene Ringworm, vectorised by Д.Ильин, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

items: Width: current flows on three faces, so each fin contributes $W = W_F + 2H_F$, with a fin width $W_F$ of a few nanometres (about 6 nm) and height $H_F$ of tens (about 50 nm).

Quantized width: $H_F$ is set by the process, and $W_F$ is fixed too because it controls series resistance, channel-length modulation and leakage. A wider device can only be made by adding fins, so $W$ comes in steps of one fin's width (for example 100 nm).
Fin spacing $S_F$ is also fixed by the process and matters for performance.
The intrinsic device is so small that gate and source/drain contacts must land away from it, on wider poly and on regions that strap the fins together, which adds resistance and capacitance.

blocks.text: The MOS structure as a capacitor
Tie source, drain and bulk of an NMOS together and the gate sees a two-terminal capacitor whose value depends on $V_{GS}$:

items: Accumulation (very negative $V_{GS}$): holes are pulled to the surface, forming a plate right under the oxide. The capacitance per area is $C_{ox}$.

Depletion and weak inversion (between about 0 and $V_{TH}$): the holes are pushed away and a depletion layer forms; the capacitance is $C_{ox}$ in series with the depletion capacitance $C_{dep}$, smaller than either.
Strong inversion ($V_{GS} > V_{TH}$): the channel forms a new plate at the surface and the capacitance returns to $C_{ox}$.

blocks.alt: Capacitance against gate-source voltage. The curve is flat at Cox for negative voltages (accumulation), dips to a minimum between zero and the threshold voltage (depletion and weak inversion) and rises back to Cox above VTH (strong inversion).
blocks.caption: C-V curve of an MOS capacitor (low-frequency behaviour, illustrative shape).

blocks.text: This voltage dependence is what makes MOS varactors work in oscillators (see LC Oscillators and VCOs), and the large capacitance per area in inversion makes a MOSFET a compact on-chip bypass capacitor, as long as it is biased well into inversion or accumulation.

blocks.title: Sizing a FinFET
blocks.text: A process has $W_F = 6\text{ nm}$ and $H_F = 50\text{ nm}$. How many fins give an effective width of at least $1\,\mu\text{m}$, and what width do you actually get?

blocks.title: Width per footprint
blocks.text: Fins with an effective width of 106 nm each are placed on a 40 nm pitch. How much channel width does a FinFET give per unit of layout width, compared with a planar device?
solution: A planar device gives 1 nm of width per nm of layout. The FinFET gives $106/40 \approx 2.65$ nm per nm, because the side walls add width vertically.
blocks.answer: About 2.65 times the planar width for the same footprint.

blocks.title: MOS capacitor in depletion
blocks.text: An MOS capacitor of $100\,\mu\text{m}^2$ has $C_{ox} = 20\text{ fF}/\mu\text{m}^2$. In depletion the depletion capacitance is $5\text{ fF}/\mu\text{m}^2$. Find the total capacitance in inversion and in depletion.
solution: Depletion: the series combination is $\frac{20 \cdot 5}{20 + 5} = 4\text{ fF}/\mu\text{m}^2$, so $0.4\text{ pF}$.
blocks.answer: 2 pF in inversion, 0.4 pF in depletion: a 5 to 1 tuning range.
